title: Engie could supply power to planned Google data center in Châteauroux, France
html:
Energy firm Engie could supply power to Google’s proposed data center near Châteauroux, France.

The companies have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) that paves the way for Engie to become Google’s preferred energy supplier and management partner, if the data center project goes ahead.

Google is looking to build on land at the Ozans Business Park, south east of Châteauroux, a city in the Indre department of France. DCD reported earlier this year that it is set to pay €58.5 million ($68m) for the site, which could host a data center of up to 500MW. It would be the hyperscaler’s first self-built data center in France.

This project is currently undergoing a public consultation process led by the Commission Nationale du Débat Public (CNDP), and as part of the MoU, Engie will “bring its technical and energy expertise to the discussions on the project’s feasibility, contributing to the public consultation process, in line with the CNDP framework.”

If the data center goes ahead, Engie and Google will work together to increase capacity in the grid through the development of “a balanced, large-scale, and multi-technology clean energy portfolio.”

The companies will also look to new grid integration and flexibility solutions, including utility-scale and behind-the-meter battery energy storage systems (BESS), as well as pledging to look at ways to keep energy bills down for residents, through investments in systems such as district heating.

“Data centers are becoming an important part of our energy systems and their development must go hand in hand with additional renewable energy generation, flexibility and close integration with local infrastructure and communities,” said Edouard Neviaski, Engie’s executive vice president in charge of supply and energy management.

“Engie can bring together its expertise across renewable power, energy management, storage and local energy infrastructures to help design an integrated approach for the Châteauroux project, working closely with Google and the local ecosystem.”

Google already works with Engie on a 24/7 carbon free energy supply deal that covers its data center operations in Germany. This partnership began in 2021 and was recently extended until 2030.

“Our proposed project in Châteauroux is designed to support the local community,” said Aris Karcanias, EMEA head of energy and infrastructure at Google. “By teaming up with ENGIE, we will explore innovative solutions in grid flexibility, clean energy generation, and energy efficiency, ensuring our data center integrates responsibly and locally.”
summary: Firms agree potential power deal that would include renewable energy investment
